headline: Google brings Gemini's personal data features to cars, updates ad privacy policy
summary: Google is expanding Gemini's Personal Intelligence feature, which taps Gmail, Calendar, Photos and other services for personalized help, to Android Auto and cars with Google built-in. Alongside this, Google updated its privacy policy to allow Gmail and Photos data to be used for ad targeting when such features are enabled, prompting outlets to differ on whether that is reassuring or concerning.

claims.statement: Google is bringing Gemini's Personal Intelligence feature to cars, letting the assistant draw on Google services for more personalized responses while driving.

sources.quote: Google is bringing a more personal version of its Gemini AI assistant to your car
Google brings Gemini Personal Intelligence to Android Auto
Google’s more personalized Gemini AI is heading to your car
Gemini's Personal Intelligence is coming to cars

claims.statement: The feature lets Gemini tap into personal Google data such as Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos and YouTube for context-based responses.

sources.quote: The latest Android Auto update lets the AI assistant tap into your Google services for context-based responses.
Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search.

claims.statement: The Android Auto rollout will also extend to cars with Google built-in in the coming months.

sources.quote: In the coming months, the feature will also roll out to cars with Google built-in.

claims.statement: Google updated its privacy policy to add an exception letting Gmail, Drive and Google Photos data be used for personalized ads when such AI features are on.

sources.quote: adds an exception to its promise about not using your Drive, Gmail, or Google Photos for personalized ads.
Turning on Personal Intelligence gives the company more data for ad targeting.

claims.statement: Ars Technica advised users it is probably time to review their Gemini privacy settings.

sources.quote: It's probably time to audit your Gemini settings.

discrepancies.explanation: ZDNet frames the new data access positively as something it is cautiously fine with, while Ars Technica frames the same access as a reason to review privacy settings and warns it feeds ad targeting.

quotes.quote: It's probably time to audit your Gemini settings.
